title: GPU congestion econ lattice exploration
content:
Purpose
This working sheet explores a lattice-style scenario grid for short-term GPU congestion events and the downstream unit economics (GPU-hours and $/1M tokens) by region. The goal is to produce a compact set of knobs we can hand to Finance and SRE for runbooks and to product for SLA/price tradeoffs. This is an exploratory, simulation-driven note (not final).

Background & motivation
- Recent bursts in US-west and EMEA have exposed a non-linear relationship between queuing (tail latency) and token cost. We want a small set of interpretable scenarios (low/med/high congestion) and an overlay of capacity policy choices (reserved-heavy, spot-heavy, mixed hedge) to estimate marginal $/1M tokens and GPU-hour burn under each.
- This doc intentionally focuses on inference-phase cost (GPU-hours, preemptions, queue time) not end-to-end developer-facing price models.

Key definitions and assumptions
- Model class: autoregressive decoder (Llama-like, 65B FP16 baseline). Token generation ceiling: 8k context typical; average generation per request in these scenarios: 128 tokens.
- GPU types: A100-80GB (hosted/dedicated) and a spot-class variant (A100-40GB equiv). Use simplified throughput buckets: 27 tok/ms for 65B FP16 baseline on A100-80GB at seq=512; 20 tok/ms on the spot-class instance due to memory/partitioning overhead.
- Workload mix: 70% short-chat (32 tokens), 25% medium (128 tokens), 5% long (512 tokens).
- Tokenization: 1 token ~= 4 chars; not critical to econ here.
- Efficiency levers modeled: batching window (10ms, 30ms, 100ms), prefix KV caching hit-rate (0%, 30%, 70%), quantization variant (FP16 / 4-bit dynamic), and preemption loss multiplier for spot (wasted compute when preempted = 0.25 of in-flight work on average).
- Regional base prices (GPU-hour, USD) used in model (approx, pre-negotiation): US-west on-demand A100-80GB = $6.8/hr, EMEA = $7.6/hr, APAC = $8.9/hr. Spot-class = on-demand * 0.38 (varies). These are placeholders; final paper should pull from pricing API.

Lattice (scenario grid) specification
- Axis A (congestion): Low (10% utilization tail), Medium (60% util), High (95% util).
- Axis B (capacity mix): Reserved-heavy (80% reserved, 20% spot), Balanced (50/50), Spot-first (20% reserved, 80% spot).
- Axis C (operational levers): Conservative (small batch=10ms, cache=0%, no quant), Practical (30ms batch, cache=30%, 4-bit), Aggressive (100ms batch, cache=70%, 4-bit + extra kernel tuning).
- This yields 27 lattice points. For each point we simulate steady-state over a 1-hour window with poisson arrivals matching utilization target, capture GPU-hour burn (including wasted work from preemptions), average latency p50/p95, and compute $/1M tokens.

Simulation model (high-level)
1) Given target utilization U and capacity mix, compute required active GPUs = ceil(requested_throughput / instance_throughput) for on-demand and spot separately, then adjust to meet U by tuning arrival rate.
2) Batching effect: throughput increases sub-linearly with batch window due to batching efficiency; we apply empiric multipliers: 10ms=1.0x, 30ms=1.18x, 100ms=1.35x to baseline token throughput.
3) Cache effect: A cache hit avoids full forward pass for prefix; we model hit as a 0.12x cost relative to full gen.
4) Spot preemption: when spot preempted, fraction f_waste of in-flight work is lost and needs redo; preemption rate scaled with spot fraction and congestion.
5) Unit cost calculation: total_cost = on_demand_gpu_hours * on_demand_price + spot_gpu_hours * spot_price + expected_waste_cost; unit $/1M tokens = (total_cost / total_tokens) * 1e6.

Representative results (extracted from the simulation)
Note: numbers are illustrative; final run will use live prices.

- Scenario A1 (Low congestion, Balanced capacity, Practical ops)
  - Utilization: 60% target, batch=30ms, cache=30%, mix=50/50
  - Active GPUs: on-demand=60, spot=60
  - GPU-hour burn (1h simulated): 118 GPU-hrs (plus 2% wasted redo on spot)
  - Cost: $6.8*60*0.5 + $6.8*0.38*60*0.5 approx = $480 + $155 = $635 (plus $12 wasted) ~ $647/hr
  - Tokens produced: 95M tokens/hr
  - $/1M tokens ≈ $6.8

- Scenario B3 (High congestion, Spot-first, Aggressive ops)
  - Utilization: 95% target, batch=100ms, cache=70%, mix=20/80 (reserved/spot)
  - Active GPUs: on-demand=40, spot=160 (more spot to hit throughput)
  - GPU-hour burn: 200 GPU-hrs (spot preemption causes 12% redo on average) -> effective burn 224 GPU-hrs accounted for cost
  - Cost: on-demand cost $6.8*40 = $272; spot cost $6.8*0.38*160 = $414; plus redo cost $27 -> total ~$713/hr
  - Tokens produced: 280M tokens/hr (batching + cache boost)
  - $/1M tokens ≈ $2.55 (lower than A1 due to aggressive batching and cache despite preemption waste)

- Scenario C2 (Medium congestion, Reserved-heavy, Conservative ops)
  - Utilization: 60% target, batch=10ms, cache=0%, mix=80/20
  - Active GPUs: on-demand=120, spot=30
  - GPU-hour burn: 150 GPU-hrs (little waste)
  - Cost: on-demand $6.8*120 = $816; spot $6.8*0.38*30 = $78; total ~$894/hr
  - Tokens produced: 100M tokens/hr
  - $/1M tokens ≈ $8.94

Interpretation notes and operational implications
- Aggressive batching + cache is the single biggest lever to reduce $/1M tokens, often outweighing the spot-discount for many scenarios. That suggests product-level knobs (max batch window, suggested cache TTL) can be used to control unit economics without exposing clients to spot preemption.
- Spot-first mixes can be cheaper in high-throughput, bursty workloads when you can tolerate redo risk, but the marginal return shrinks when preemption waste grows with congestion. We should calculate a breakeven preemption rate for each region (currently ~9–14% in our quick sims).
- Reserved-heavy profiles stabilize tail latency and reduce waste; they are appropriate for SLA-backed Dedicated tiers despite higher $/1M tokens.
- Regional price differentials matter: APAC premium (>20% higher in our crude pricing) shifts the optimal mix toward batching+cache before spot increases.

Next steps and action items
- Run the lattice with the live pricing API and weekly spot availability traces (ENGINF-482) and produce a canonical table of $/1M tokens by region for the sales playbook. Owner: Evan. Due: 2025-02-07.
- Hook this simulation to the capacity runbook generator so that for a requested SLO and throughput we can recommend mix + batch/cache profile (PR in infra repo: #915). Owner: María. Due: 2025-02-21.
- Add a column to Dedicated pricing proposals that shows expected $/1M tokens under Conservative / Practical / Aggressive ops for customer transparency. Owner: Zoe. Due: 2025-03-03.

Appendix: quick sensitivity snippets
- If A100 on-demand rises 15% in a region, $/1M tokens increases ~10–12% for conservative ops, but only ~5% for aggressive ops thanks to batch/caching elasticity.
- Increasing cache hit-rate from 30% to 70% reduces GPU-hour burn by ~18% in median workloads in our model.
- Preemption waste elasticity: every +5% absolute spot preemption rate increases $/1M tokens by ~0.25–0.6 in spot-heavy mixes depending on batching.

Notes-to-self (unresolved)
- Need to model multi-model packing effects (two smaller models on one card) for long-tail microservice requests.
- Incorporate cold-start overhead for model loading in Private deployments.
- Validate throughput multipliers for quantized kernels on the 65B model under mixed-seq lengths.

End of sheet.
